messages:
Maya: kicking off emberling-v1 bring-up in onboarding suite. quick sanity: recall@1=0.63, recall@5=0.82 on short-query holdout. silhouette down ~0.04 vs aurora baseline. lower latency though (1.8x tokens/s). any quick ideas? :thinking_face:
Anuj: what's the baseline numbers and eval set exactly?
Maya: baseline is aurora-embed-v2 fp16: recall@1=0.68, recall@5=0.85 on the same 50k short-query holdout we use for onboarding. eval set = short_queries_50k_v2 (50k queries, mixed domains).
Liam: did you try int8 quant yet or only fp16?
Maya: ran a couple. fp16 -> recall@1 0.63. int8 per-tensor -> 0.59, int8 per-channel -> 0.625. used ONNX path with dynamic quant. command: ```bash
./run_eval --model emberling:v1 --quant per_channel --batch 64 --holdout short_queries_50k_v2
```
Dana: can you paste centroid / manifold diffs? curious if it's a global shift or particular classes.
Maya: quick numbers: avg centroid L2 shift = 0.12 (baseline 0.05). affected label groups top3 = ["how-to", "api-reference", "cli-usage"]. silhouette score delta (emberling - baseline) = -0.04 overall, but varies by class.
ops-bot: CI: embed-eval/4249876543 completed: smoke ✅ latency OK, cost profiling attached. Artifacts: https://ci.redwood.ai/embeds/4249876543
Anuj: thanks. can we try hybrid quant (mixed 8/4) or per-channel int4 calibration? also run recall@10 and long-query holdout (long_queries_10k).
Maya: scheduling three runs now: (A) int4 hybrid per-channel calibration, (B) longer-query holdout, (C) kmeans k=100 centroid drift test + nn-ID-flip.
Liam: if centroid shift persists consider small in-domain fine-tune (2k steps) or a linear projection recalibration layer on top. cheap and often fixes neighborhood shifts.
Dana: also add silhouette_by_class, nn-idflip(k=1,5) and recall stratified by query length. I'll notify data-team for extra labels.
Maya: noted. starting runs — will post partials in ~2h. :thumbsup:
(2h later) Maya: results update: int4-hybrid per-channel (calibrated) => recall@1 0.642, recall@5 0.83 on short-query holdout. recall@10 0.88. long-queries: recall@1 0.60 (baseline long 0.66). silhouette delta improved to -0.01 overall. centroid avg shift down to 0.07. nn-idflip@1 dropped from 0.11 -> 0.08 (better).
Anuj: int4 hybrid numbers look promising — small gap to baseline and big perf/cost win? what's latency difference?
Maya: latency: fp16 p99 = 42ms, int4-hybrid p99 = 26ms on same batch/infra. cost/unit estimate ~35% lower.
Liam: can we run a canary A/B on dedicated lane with 5% traffic and run production queries for 24h? watch recall@1 drift and user-facing metrics.
Dana: I'll open rollout ticket with canary plan + SLIs (recall@1, nn-idflip, latency p99). also add alert: if recall@1 drops >0.02 vs baseline for 30m -> automatic rollback.
Maya: starting canary config and smoke tests. ops-bot: deploy request when ready.
ops-bot: noted — canary pool available in us-west-2 dedicated. follow deploy checklist: `canary-config.yaml` + eval snapshot.
Anuj: also add regression alert for embedding eval pipeline: if any onboarding model recall@1 falls >0.03 vs pinned baseline, create incident-cha.
Maya: will push final artifacts and plots (UMAPs, kmeans hits, per-class silhouette table). posting links shortly.
Liam: great work — if A/B is stable we can promote and add quant profile to model catalog.
Dana: I'll draft release notes mentioning int4-hybrid tradeoffs and recommended fallback to fp16.
Maya: done for now — will update with artifacts. :rocket:
